title: Machine learning model for early bone metastasis diagnosis in non-small cell lung cancer
summary: Six machine-learning models on routine serum indicators in 664 stage IV NSCLC patients were compared, and a random forest on 11 selected indicators was best. It reached an AUC of 0.98 (0.95-0.99) on internal and 0.97 (0.94-0.99) on external validation (113 patients) and also predicted bone metastasis during follow-up of 316 patients. Possible overlap between external and prospective patients and the timing of model locking were not confirmed; single-region Chinese cohorts.
ai_technology: Random forest (best of six machine-learning models) on serum indicators
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital

evidence.tested: Derivation cohort of 664, external cohort of 113 and follow-up of 316 patients for at least two years.
evidence.unknown: Whether the model was frozen before the follow-up cohort; generalisability beyond the cohorts.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning built the diagnostic model from serum indicators.
